A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by Levin and Alterman. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, references and appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-volume and Monte Carlo simulations, together with fitting and focusing results from lab-acquired parafilm, mouse-brain and chicken-breast transmission matrices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations and laboratory results, including in Supplement C, and reports additional layer-count, thickness and optical-depth comparisons.

M1.justification: The multi-slice propagation model, weak-scattering approximation and gradient-descent fitting procedure remain unchanged. Equations 2 and 4 retain the same components and operations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate uniform-spectrum and random-sphere synthetic volumes, Monte Carlo scattering, and parafilm, mouse-brain and chicken-breast samples. The revised thickness, optical-depth and spatial-support settings remain within this existing material and task coverage.

E2.justification: The filtering-versus-optimization comparison is retained from v1 Figure 4 in v2 Figure 9, alongside the zero-layer ballistic reference. No additional cited method becomes an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: v2 Figure 3 reports paired optical-depth settings at fixed thickness: 16 µm with OD 0.5/2 and 32 µm with OD 1/4. Figure 5 also reports a 13 × 13 µm chicken-breast support, whereas v1 Figure 10 and v2 Figure 14 report 25 × 25 µm. Conflicting captions and references leave the relationship between these laboratory settings unclear.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 3 adds fixed-support reconstructions using 32, 8 and 4 layers and a comparison separating thickness effects from optical-depth effects. The two support-sweep panels in v1 Figure 7 become one panel in v2 Figure 4(f). Most spectral, Monte Carlo and focusing diagnostics are retained in the supplement.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental replicate counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added curves retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds Figure 3's sensitivity results and Figure 5's 13 × 13 µm example, while removing v1 Table 1's compression ratios. Synthetic field-of-view gains are corrected from 16×/100× to 4×/25×. The laboratory narrative reports an 18× gain under revised supports, while Supplement C.2 retains the earlier approximately 150× claim; these are not comparable same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The Nyquist derivation, quadratic fitting-error bound and proof are retained, principally in Supplement A. The limited mathematical removal is v1's explicit NM degrees-of-freedom argument for representing an N-by-N transmission matrix with M layers, accompanying the removal of the compression analysis.

C1.justification: The central claims about missing-cone-enabled sparse fitting and expanded correction fields remain. v2 removes transmission-matrix compression as an explicit contribution from the introduction and discussion, concentrating the contribution on practical wavefront-shaping applications.

C2.justification: v2 adds relay-system and reversed-layer-order constraints and explicitly anticipates needing dozens of layers for broad correction through thick tissue. It interprets the new comparison as showing greater sensitivity to thickness than optical depth. Conversely, it removes v1's mean-free-path explanation of when naive filtering fails.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-and-data access link and specifies 0.5 µm axial spacing for the dense reconstruction example. It omits v1's explicit 81² illumination-grid size and 0.5 µm transverse sampling pitch. Most acquisition and volume-synthesis details remain in Supplements C and D.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially recasts the research context around computational imaging, confocal/OCT methods and adaptive optics, replacing much of the earlier transmission-matrix and tomography survey. It explicitly credits Hua et al. (2023) as inspiration and adds substantial adaptive-optics and Born/Rytov background.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. An experiments-first main narrative replaces v1's theory-first Results section, while large portions of the analysis, empirical evaluation and methods move into Supplements A–D, with some explanatory material repeated.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is substantially redrawn, new reconstruction composites are introduced, existing images and curves are regrouped, and many figures move into the supplement. Table 1 is removed. Axes, legends and captions also change, including inconsistent support labels in Figure 5.

improvement.justification: The controlled thickness-versus-optical-depth comparison, corrected synthetic field-of-view gains and code/data pointer provide modest improvements in evidence and reproducibility information. The application-focused organization also clarifies the practical motivation. These gains are limited by conflicting chicken-breast support descriptions in Figure 5, its caption and Supplement C.2/Figure 14, and by omitted sampling details.
